title: Ensemble Reconstruction of the Kuroshio Current During the Last Glacial Maximum Using an Eddy‐Resolving OGCM
content:
Abstract

The Last Glacial Maximum (LGM), the coldest phase of the last glacial cycle, was characterized by a pronounced sea-level drop and millennial-scale climate variability. These large-scale changes likely induced substantial shifts in the path and transport of the Kuroshio Current, the principal western boundary current of the North Pacific subtropical gyre. However, its detailed glacial configuration remains poorly constrained due to limited observations and incomplete model representations. Here, we applied sea surface forcings from 10 paleoclimate models in the Paleoclimate Modelling Intercomparison Project (PMIP) to an eddy-resolving (1/12°) Ocean General Circulation Model (OGCM), the Japan Coastal Ocean Predictability Experiment for Paleo-ocean (JCOPE-P), to perform ensemble simulations of the Kuroshio during LGM. The ensemble mean suggests that the Kuroshio continued to enter the Okinawa Trough east of Taiwan but shifted seaward within the East China Sea in response to the sea-level drop during LGM. In the Kuroshio Extension region, the current axis migrated southward, primarily driven by a southward displacement of the zero line of wind stress curl. Kuroshio transport during LGM also likely exceeded that in modern ocean, largely due to intensified basin-scale wind stress curl that enhanced the southward Sverdrup transport. Additionally, the ensemble simulations refined the heterogeneous cooling of sea surface temperatures (SSTs) in the Kuroshio region. Overall, the results align well with proxy-based SST reconstructions, indicating that the ensemble simulations are dynamically constrained and provide a robust framework for understanding glacial oceanographic changes.
